headline: Wild place Jared Spurgeon on injured reserve
take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Wild have placed Jared Spurgeon on injured reserve, noting he has missed the past couple of games with an upper-body injury.

The Wild can ill afford to lose him, even if his box score looks modest. Spurgeon has played 22.36 minutes a game, and in his 6 games so far this season the Wild have controlled 60.21 percent of the 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice. Their share of the game is 12.47 percentage points better with him than without, a big swing for a defenseman. His one goal and four assists have come on just 0.18 expected goals of his own, so he is running 0.82 goals above what his chances would predict, and that finishing will cool. His value is in driving play, not scoring. Minnesota sits at 5-2-1 with 11 points, but the underlying picture is thinner: a 50 percent 5-on-5 expected goals share, and 3.9 goals saved above expected by the goaltending is doing real work. Without Spurgeon's minutes, that margin gets harder to hold.
